body.statement:
Suppose \(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0\le1/2\).  For every \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) there are constants \(c_\alpha>0\) and \(\eta_\alpha>2\alpha\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(T\), the base Holder model class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) contains two laws with the same interior realized path whose observed-data laws possess a common subprobability measure of mass at least \(\eta_\alpha\), while their causal targets differ by at least
\[
 c_\alpha\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\]
Both laws satisfy the frozen geometric beta-mixing envelope and the design-conditional centering assumption.  No lower local-modulus condition is used.
body.justification: The rare-cluster bump is a direct base-Holder witness for the logarithmic spacing penalty.
body.gap: Ordinary i.i.d. spacing arguments do not control triangular-array clustering of a shrinking target neighborhood.
body.consumer: The marginal and honest-length lower bounds use its common-submeasure certificate.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(q=Sd\).  The condition \(B^4\ge q^2\) permits a common donor law \(Z_j=z_0+U_j\), where the coordinates of \(U_j\) are independent Rademacher variables.  It has mean \(z_0\), covariance \(I_q\), and standardized fourth moment \(q^2\); it is independent of all panel variables below.

Choose \(\gamma>0\) so small that \(e^{-\gamma}>2\alpha\), and set
\[
 L_T=\left\lfloor
 \frac{\log T-2\log\log(T\vee3)}{|\log\rho_0|}
 \right\rfloor\vee1,
 \qquad p_T=\frac{\gamma L_T}{T}.
\tag{1}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
 2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
Partition the first cohort's calendar into complete consecutive blocks of length \(L_T\).  Independently label each complete block by \(C_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Let \(A_T\) be a cube centered at \(z_{01}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_d\) of volume \(p_T\).  Conditional on \(C_b=1\), draw all design points in block \(b\) independently uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(C_b=0\), draw them independently uniformly on its complement.  Thus at every complete-block time the marginal density is exactly
\[
 p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
 +(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1.
\tag{3}
\]
Draw the incomplete block and the other cohorts independently and uniformly.

If \(k<L_T\), past and future sigma-fields separated by \(k\) indices can share at most one block label.  Replacing that label by an independent copy fails with probability at most \(2p_T\), so \(\beta(k)\le2p_T\); if \(k\ge L_T\), the relevant labels are disjoint and \(\beta(k)=0\).  Equation (2) therefore gives
\[
 \beta(k)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\qquad(k\ge1).
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(E_T\) be the event that every complete block has label zero and that no point of the incomplete block falls in a fixed smaller concentric cube.  Since the incomplete block has fewer than \(L_T\) observations, its extra failure probability is at most \(L_Tp_T=o(1)\), while
\[
 \Pr(E_T)=(1-p_T)^{\lfloor T/L_T\rfloor}-o(1)
 \longrightarrow e^{-\gamma}=:\eta_\alpha>2\alpha.
\tag{5}
\]
Let \(h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}\) be the side scale of that smaller cube and take a fixed smooth bump \(\phi\), supported on the unit ball, with \(\phi(0)=1\).  For a sufficiently small fixed \(a>0\), define
\[
 m_{10}(x)=b_0,\qquad
 m_{11}(x)=b_0+a h_T^\lambda
 \phi((x-z_{01})/h_T),
\tag{6}
\]
and keep all other cohort surfaces equal to \(b_0\).  Holder scaling makes the \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) norm of the added bump bounded uniformly in \(T\); choosing \(a,b_0\) small enforces both the Holder radius and bounded wealth.

Under alternative \(v\), set \(Q_{1ti}=m_{1v}(X_{1t})\), use the common constant surfaces in other cohorts, keep positive treated observations identical, impose consistency, and set the unobserved untreated event wealth equal to \(m_{sv}(z_{0s})\).  Choose all amplitudes so these levels lie in \((0,B)\), and realize each as in \texttt{def:buyhold-level} by taking \(W_{si,-1}=1\), \(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), and all later returns zero.  Then design-conditional centering and event-date transport are exact, cross-unit independence holds, and the joint design--response sequence inherits (4).  On \(E_T\), every observed response lies outside the bump support, so the restrictions of the two observed laws to \(E_T\) coincide.  They consequently possess a common subprobability measure of mass at least \(\eta_\alpha\) for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Finally, \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (6) give
\[
 |\tau_1(z_0)-\tau_0(z_0)|
 =\pi_1a h_T^\lambda
 \asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\tag{7}
\]
This proves the certificate over the base Holder class.
